blocks.text: 1. LeNet
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474320-532636337.png

Separable Convolution, the final topic of the previous CNN module, closed out coverage of the fundamental building blocks. LeNet opens the CNN Architectures module as the genuinely earliest influential design combining those blocks into a complete network.
It is a genuinely small, complete network combining convolution and pooling layers already covered, explored in full historical and structural depth throughout this topic.
2. Historical Context

A genuinely important historical note connects back to History, already covered in the Introduction to Deep Learning module. LeNet, developed for recognizing handwritten digits, predates the modern deep learning era by decades.

This genuinely early origin makes LeNet a genuinely fascinating starting point for this module, demonstrating the core ideas already covered throughout the CNN module long before they became widely popular.
3. The Overall Structure
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474321-179095132.png

This connects back to every building block already covered throughout the CNN module. LeNet alternates convolutional layers and pooling layers, then ends with fully connected layers, following a genuinely clear, sequential design.
This is exactly the transition-to-classifier pattern already covered in Flattening, with LeNet standing as one of the genuinely earliest concrete examples of that exact pattern in practice.

blocks.text: 4. The Choice Of Small Filters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474321-984884304.png

This connects back to filter size, already covered in Filters and Kernels. LeNet uses genuinely small filters throughout, keeping receptive fields modest at each stage, consistent with the small filter convention already covered there.
These receptive fields grow gradually across layers, already covered in Receptive Field, following the exact same accumulation mechanism already covered in that earlier topic.
5. The Choice Of Average Pooling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474321-960558193.png

This connects back to Average Pooling, already covered in its own topic. LeNet genuinely used Average Pooling, an older choice predating Max Pooling's own later popularity, already covered in its own dedicated topic.

This is a genuinely interesting historical detail, since Max Pooling later became the more common default across most modern Convolutional Neural Network architectures, already covered in Max Pooling.

blocks.text: 6. A Parameter Count Perspective
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474322-703489869.png
This connects back to Network Architecture, already covered in its own topic. By modern standards, LeNet is genuinely tiny, with far fewer parameters than any network covered later in this module.

This is a genuinely useful baseline for appreciating how much scale has grown since, setting up a genuinely direct point of comparison against the much larger, deeper architectures covered throughout the rest of this module.
7. Why LeNet Genuinely Matters Historically
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474322-592266183.png

A genuinely important legacy connects back to the core building blocks already covered throughout the CNN module. LeNet genuinely demonstrated that these building blocks, combined together, could learn real, practical visual tasks.

This genuinely proved the core Convolutional Neural Network concept long before the computational resources existed to scale it up dramatically, a legacy that directly shaped every architecture covered later in this module.
8. A Genuine Limitation By Today's Standard

blocks.alt: A Genuine Limitation By Today's Standard
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445474322-908621406.png
A genuinely honest, real limitation connects back to genuinely large, complex images, unlike LeNet's own small, simple digit images that it was originally designed for.
LeNet's genuinely shallow depth and small scale make it unsuited to today's genuinely harder visual tasks, exactly the gap that every architecture covered later in this module was designed to close.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Studying LeNet Is Genuinely Still Worthwhile

Understanding the genuinely foundational pattern that every later architecture in this module builds upon is a direct case for studying LeNet, already covered in this topic, the genuinely clearest, simplest place to see that pattern first.

Genuinely small, simple classification tasks with genuinely limited data or compute are another genuine case where a LeNet-like design, already covered, can still genuinely be a reasonable, practical starting point.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates LeNet's own overall structure in code, showing the alternating convolution and pooling pattern already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
# A genuinely simplified sketch of LeNet's own layer sequence, already covered as the overall structure in this topic
lenet_layers = [
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 6, "filter_size": 5},   # already covered as the choice of small filters
    {"type": "avg_pool", "pool_size": 2},                # already covered as the choice of Average Pooling
    {"type": "conv", "filters": 16, "filter_size": 5},
    {"type": "avg_pool", "pool_size": 2},
    {"type": "flatten"},                                  # already covered in Flattening
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 120},
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 84},
    {"type": "fully_connected", "units": 10},             # 10 digit classes, already covered as its original task
]

total_conv_layers = sum(1 for layer in lenet_layers if layer["type"] == "conv")
total_pool_layers = sum(1 for layer in lenet_layers if layer["type"] == "avg_pool")
total_fc_layers = sum(1 for layer in lenet_layers if layer["type"] == "fully_connected")

print(f"LeNet's overall structure: {total_conv_layers} convolutional layers, {total_pool_layers} pooling layers, {total_fc_layers} fully connected layers")
print("Notice the alternating pattern already covered as this topic's own overall structure")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: LeNet is an early, influential Convolutional Neural Network for handwritten digit recognition.
It predates the modern deep learning era by decades.
It alternates convolutional and pooling layers, then ends with fully connected layers.
It uses genuinely small filters throughout, keeping receptive fields modest at each stage.
It historically used Average Pooling, before Max Pooling became the more common default.
By modern standards, it is genuinely tiny, with far fewer parameters than later architectures.
It proved that convolution and pooling building blocks could learn real, practical visual tasks.
Its shallow depth and small scale make it unsuited to today's harder, larger visual tasks.
Next up: AlexNet, the architecture that helped launch the modern deep learning era.
